usage: ‘ting1 jat6’ means 'tomorrow' and is used to talk about the day after today.
It is commonly placed at the beginning or end of a sentence to specify the time when something will happen.
‘ting1 jat6’ can be used with verbs to indicate future actions or plans.
It is an informal, everyday way to say ‘tomorrow’ in spoken Cantonese.
You can also use ‘ting1 jat6 mou5 gin3’ to mean 'see you tomorrow'.

examples.meaning: I will go to work tomorrow.

examples.jyutping: nei5 ting1 jat6 jau5 mou5 si4 gaan3?
ting1 jat6 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 sik6 faan6 laa1.
nei5 ting1 jat6 gei2 dim2 faan1 lai4?
examples.meaning: What time will you come back tomorrow?
